title: Complete Introduction to New Features of CLO7.3 Patch Version (Latest Update January 30, 2024)
description: CLO7.3 Latest Update Released! Proudly Introducing EveryWear and Brand-New AI Features to Further Enhance Your Design Experience!
transcript:
Hello everyone, today I would like to introduce you to Clo 7.3, a new feature designed in the updated version 30 days later.  
There are seven modules in total, which are the main functions, 2D, 3D, virtual model, color, rendering, and mode.  
First of all, let's talk about the main function, Everywhere.  
From the beginning, the Everywhere function can be easily optimized in Clo for various digital spaces, such as games, the round universe, and entertainment spaces.  
The Everywhere function is currently in the testing stage, and all users who pre-register on the Connect web page can use it.  
Pre-registration can be done on the Connect web page Everywhere option and is unlimited and open.  
Please note that Everywhere is a test function.  
The policy of use may change in the future.  
In this example, we will guide you to use Everywhere to complete the process of testing clothes, network optimization, binding skeleton, UV fill, and baking pattern.  
In the software interface, click on the icon in the upper right corner to open Everywhere.  
The Everywhere window appears in the upper right corner of the 2D version of the test window.  
The number of multidirectional network spaces for clothes and virtual models is displayed in the lower left corner of the 3D window.  
The Everywhere window is divided into two options, clothes and materials.  
In the clothes option, you can optimize the multidirectional network space and bind the skeleton.  
In the material option, you can perform operations such as UV filling, baking pattern, and material application.  
First, let's take a look at the multidirectional network optimization in the clothing option.  
Multidirectional refers to the network that constitutes the clothing.  
When you share your creations on different platforms, the number and capacity of the support network may be different.  
Therefore, considering the different functions of each platform, you can use the multidirectional network optimization function to maintain the 3D clothing form.  
At the same time, the optimization of the multidirectional network number is effective.  
Before the optimization process is carried out, you can check the total network space of the current clothing.  
In the Everywhere window, the number on the right side of the clothing indicates the current network space of the clothing.  
This number includes the number of buttons or accessories on the clothing.  
In addition, in the next virtual model column, you can check the multidirectional network space of the virtual model.  
In addition, in the lower left corner of the 3D window, you can verify the number of multidirectional network spaces.  
Here you can check the number of multidirectional network spaces for the version and the accessory.  
How to optimize the multidirectional network:  
First, in the clothing option in the multidirectional network optimization, enter the required multidirectional network number in the blank box on the left.  
Then click optimize.  
Apply the customized multidirectional network to the specified number.  
If the accessory or button is a high-quality model, it can be done individually.  
Then click OK.  
You can optimize the individual optimization.  
For the individual optimization of the accessory, you need to select the button or accessory to be used in the material window.  
After selecting, enter the required value into the technology box in the multidirectional network optimization at the bottom of the attribute editor window.  
This will optimize the multidirectional network of the accessory to be matched to the specified number.  
Next, I will explain the option of binding the skeleton.  
First, the binding skeleton is in the 3D virtual model.  
It is a process of creating a similar skeleton structure so that it can be linked and moved.  
In the binding skeleton function of Everywhere, the binding skeleton can promote the synchronization of the created clothing and virtual model.  
This design will connect the skeleton joints of the created virtual model with the clothing, ensuring that the movement of the clothing and virtual model are synchronized.  
The binding skeleton of Everywhere is specifically suitable for the human virtual model with joints.  
And when the virtual model is in A or T-shape, it can run effectively.  
Under these conditions, the Binding Google function will automatically bind the clothing according to the binding information in the virtual model.  
Click the App button in the Binding Google column to apply the Binding Google function.  
To confirm whether the Binding Google function is applied, we apply a few poses.  
As you can see, once the Binding Google function is completed, the crowd will be applied to the clothing, allowing it to be switched with the virtual model during the pose change.  
When you apply a different pose, you can observe the seamless switching between the clothing and the virtual model.  
At this time, please note that when the Binding Google function is applied, a warning message will appear, as shown in the slide.  
If you choose Yes, the clothing will be simulated.

You can see that the sticker is not only displayed in the 2D version, but also visible outside.  
And only by using the adjustment sticker tool, you can select the sticker in the 2D window or 3D window, so that it can display all, otherwise the sticker is not visible in the part outside the version.  
Through the improved function, we can rotate the sticker and check the sticker in different colors more easily.  
In addition, we have added the option of adding and deleting all unused items.  
In the new version, the items that are not assigned and unused in the 3D window can be deleted at once.  
This option can be used for all object objects in the 3D window.  
For example, let's see the button in the 3D window.  
You can see that there are four buttons in these buttons that have not been used, and two of them are applied to the costume.  
On the unused button, click on the button on the right, and select the button to delete all unused buttons from the list.  
You can see that the unused items will be deleted.  
This can help us to manage unused items more effectively.  
Next is the update about rendering.  
In the new version, we added the option of controlling the size of the round top in the skylight attribute.  
We can find the round top parameters of the skylight in the rendering light setting, by adjusting the size of the round top light to adapt the scene.  
First, open the light line attribute in the rendering window, and open the round top size.  
This makes a gap in the background when moving the camera.  
When you need to direct the light pattern to the ground, this is very useful.  
The round top control is basically made up of three parts, the bottom of the hemisphere, the ground, and the transition area between the two.  
First is the radius parameter.  
As the value increases, the radius of the whole round top becomes wider.  
The smallest value is 1 meter.  
When the value is set to the smallest value, you can see that the radius of the light also becomes narrower.  
At this time, you can see that the upper end of the virtual model and the costume are not lighted.  
Here the default value is 4 meters.  
Next is the ground projection height.  
If you increase the value, you will see that the image of the ground surface at the bottom will rise to the top of the hemisphere.  
Accordingly, the projection value of the light will also change.  
Therefore, you can see that the light reflected on the virtual model will also change.  
Here the default value is 1 meter.  
Finally, it is the ground mixing option.  
If you increase the value, you will see that the ground surface at the bottom and the hemisphere top will be roundly mixed together, and the shape of the transition area will change.  
Here the default value is 0.5.  
If you want to save the original size of the change, you can save all the optical properties as vrp files, or click on the file storage in the top left-hand column to save all the rendering properties as zvrp files.  
Next is about the update and improvement of the animation.  
In the new version, it is more convenient to edit the animation frame and the selection in the animation.  
First, in the new version, it is more convenient to adjust the frame rate in the animation.  
When we stop the mouse at the end of the slide at the bottom, it will display in the blue color.  
Drag the slide can manually control the frame rate of the animation slide.  
You can also enlarge the specific frame rate you want in the timeline to edit the key frame.  
If you want to display the entire animation frame in the timeline, you can double-click the slide bar at the bottom, or click the button on the far right of the bottom to adjust the animation frame range.  
The smallest and largest frames displayed on the timeline and the change area will be set to the same number of frames for the entire animation frame, so that you can check all the frames at once.  
In addition, when you export the costume file with the animation as an alembic file, you can use the current frame option to only export a single frame.  
First, on the timeline, place the playhead to the frame you want to extract, or enter the corresponding value directly in the current frame.  
Then, in the main menu, find the file, export, alembic og awa.  
In the export alembic window, select the animation menu, and select the current frame option.  
In this way, only one frame will be exported, and all other animation data will be deleted.

chunks.content: # Complete Introduction to New Features of CLO 7.3 Patch Version (Latest Update January 30, 2024) This document details the new features and technical enhancements introduced in CLO 7.3, focusing on the Everywhere function, multidirectional network optimization, skeleton binding, UV editing, material management, 2D and 3D function optimizations, rendering improvements, and animation editing upgrades. --- ## Everywhere Function: Overview and Usage This section covers the **Everywhere function**, a new feature in CLO 7.3 designed for digital spaces optimization, including games, metaverse, and entertainment environments. It explains how to access and use Everywhere for clothing testing, network optimization, skeleton binding, UV filling, and baking patterns. - **Availability**: Everywhere is currently in the testing phase and accessible to users who pre-register on the Connect webpage. Usage policies may change. - **Interface**: Access Everywhere via the icon in the upper right corner; the Everywhere window appears in the 2D test window’s upper right corner. - **Window Options**: Divided into two tabs: - **Clothes**: Optimize multidirectional networks and bind skeletons. - **Materials**: Perform UV fill, bake patterns, and apply materials. ### Multidirectional Network Optimization - **Definition**: Multidirectional networks constitute the clothing's mesh structure, vital for sharing creations across platforms with varying network support. - **Purpose**: Optimizes network size and count to maintain 3D clothing shape while reducing file size. - **Checking Network Space**: Displayed in Everywhere window beside clothing and virtual model names, and in the lower-left corner of the 3D window. - **Optimization Process**: 1. Enter desired multidirectional network number in the input box. 2. Click **Optimize** to apply. 3. For accessories or buttons, optimize individually by selecting them in the materials window and entering a specific network value in the attribute editor. 4. Confirm with **OK**. ### Skeleton Binding (Binding Google) - **Purpose**: Synchronizes the clothing’s skeleton with the virtual model skeleton to ensure coordinated movement. - **Applicability**: Best suited for human virtual models in T or A-pose. - **Procedure**: 1. Click the **App** button in the Binding Google column to apply automatic binding. 2. Test by applying different poses to check seamless clothing-model synchronization. - **Warning Message**: - Choosing **Yes** deletes Binding Google information but simulates clothing. - Choosing **No** simulates clothing while retaining Binding Google data. - **Post-Application Options**: - **Update** button re-applies binding based on current state. - **Brush Tool** enables fine-tuning of weight distribution and joint influence. ### Brush Tool for Skeleton Binding - **Activation**: Clicking the brush icon temporarily closes Everywhere and opens a brush interface showing 3D clothing with white texture and visible joints. - **Usage**: - Modify how different clothing parts respond to virtual model joint movements. - Use **Ctrl + click** to select joints and view weight distribution. - **Brush Modes**: - **Weight**: Adjusts joint influence on clothing mesh. - **Carving**: Alters surface shape of the mesh without affecting weight. - **Weight Brush Options**: - Increase, decrease, and smooth weights. - Adjustable strength, size (via slider or bracket keys), hardness, and depth. - **Weight Visualization**: - Red areas indicate high weight (more influence).
chunks.content_description: CLO7.3 Latest Update Released! Proudly Introducing EveryWear and Brand-New AI Features to Further Enhance Your Design Experience!

chunks.title: Complete Introduction to New Features of CLO7.3 Patch Version (Latest Update January 30, 2024)
chunks.content: - **Usage**: - Modify how different clothing parts respond to virtual model joint movements. - Use **Ctrl + click** to select joints and view weight distribution. - **Brush Modes**: - **Weight**: Adjusts joint influence on clothing mesh. - **Carving**: Alters surface shape of the mesh without affecting weight. - **Weight Brush Options**: - Increase, decrease, and smooth weights. - Adjustable strength, size (via slider or bracket keys), hardness, and depth. - **Weight Visualization**: - Red areas indicate high weight (more influence). - Blue areas indicate low weight. - No color means zero weight. - **Weight Hammer**: - Press **Shift + click** on problem points to smooth weight differences with adjacent areas. - **Lock Joint Function**: - Prevents specific joints from affecting mesh weight during adjustments. - **Alt + click** to lock/unlock single joint (red highlight indicates locked). - **Alt + right-click** to lock/unlock all joints. ### Carving Brush - **Purpose**: Modify clothing surface topology after automatic binding. - **Types**: - **Carving**: Pulls or pushes mesh surface, useful for fixing overlaps or adjusting tight areas. - **Flat Brush**: Softens rigid areas, making surfaces flatter and more uniform. - **Controls**: - Switch between carving and flat modes using **Ctrl + Tab**. - Adjust strength, size, hardness, and depth similar to weight brush. --- ## UV Editing and Material Management This section explains the **UV fill function**, backup textures, sticker management, and material handling. ### UV Fill Function - **Definition**: UV refers to unwrapping a 3D model surface into a 2D coordinate space for texturing. - **UV Fill**: Automatically arranges UV coordinates to avoid overlaps, optimizing texture usage. - **Interface Settings**: - **Fill Ratio**: Ratio of UV area to bounding square (default 95; range 80-100). Higher values increase fill quality but take longer. - **Rotation**: Allows UV islands to rotate during filling. - **Fixed Ratio**: Maintains aspect ratio between UV islands. - **Overall Size**: Controls UV map scaling (0 to 1). - **Selected Frame**: Specify frame for selected UVs. - **Usage**: 1. Click **Fill UV** in the upper right corner to open the UV fill window. 2. Set options and apply to fill UVs. 3. Exit to return to Everywhere window. ### Backup Texture and Multi-Layer Grid Optimization - **Backup Texture**: Generates texture stickers for high-detail appearance on optimized low-poly models, improving workflow efficiency. - **Types of Stickers**: - **Detailed Hairline Sticker**: Simulates fine surface details without extra mesh density. - **Environment Light Block Sticker**: Shows shadow and lighting effects by tracking environmental light. - **Settings**: - Adjust the number of light rays per pixel for environment light block stickers (higher number improves quality but increases calculation time). - Adjust sticker intensity values (0 to 200, default 100). - **Controls**: - Preview stickers in 3D window. - Delete stickers using the trash icon. ### Material Management - Materials correspond to UV frames and can be created, copied, renamed, or deleted. - Apply materials to clothing versions using the application button. - Only unused materials can be deleted.
chunks.content_description: CLO7.3 Latest Update Released! Proudly Introducing EveryWear and Brand-New AI Features to Further Enhance Your Design Experience!

chunks.title: Complete Introduction to New Features of CLO7.3 Patch Version (Latest Update January 30, 2024)
chunks.content: - **Settings**: - Adjust the number of light rays per pixel for environment light block stickers (higher number improves quality but increases calculation time). - Adjust sticker intensity values (0 to 200, default 100). - **Controls**: - Preview stickers in 3D window. - Delete stickers using the trash icon. ### Material Management - Materials correspond to UV frames and can be created, copied, renamed, or deleted. - Apply materials to clothing versions using the application button. - Only unused materials can be deleted. - Upload completed costumes to Connect with upload validation requiring: 1. Virtual model with joints visible in 3D. 2. All versions bound to Google. 3. All UVs filled with one frame per UV. 4. Detailed back drawings. - Upload process: - Opens FBX settings window. - After upload, FBX and ZPRJ files can be downloaded from the Connect project page. - Save progress as project files (.ZPRJ) preserving all Everywhere window configurations. --- ## 2D Function Optimizations This section describes improvements in **link editing**, **format copying**, and **core code editing** for 2D patterns. ### Link Direction Confirmation - New visual arrows indicate link directions on selected lines. - Use **Shift + select** to choose multiple links. - Right-click menu shows link settings and directions. - Helps quickly identify and adjust link directions. ### Format Copying Enhancements - Copy/paste code values for buttons and eyes directly in the 2D editor. - Can copy and paste individual x or y coordinate values without affecting the other. - Copy/paste operations now support entire line units, simplifying bulk edits. - When modifying core code size (S, M, L), changes persist across sizes without re-editing. ### Core Code Layer Editing - Core code divided into separate editable sections for inside and outside layers. - Allows selective deletion and editing without affecting entire lines. - Core code now visible and editable in the 2D board window, enabling direct comparison and adjustment. - Changes in core code immediately reflect in simulation. --- ## 3D Function Improvements This section covers **symmetrical panel application**, **3D model visibility control**, and multidirectional grid optimization. ### Symmetrical Panel Simulation - Allows applying simulation from one panel to its symmetrical counterpart. - Retains original shrink lines. - Warning appears if non-symmetrical panels are selected. - Applicable only to symmetrical panels in the 3D model. ### 3D Model Try-On Visibility - New toggle to show/hide the 3D model wearing the suit. - Accessible via the 3D window digital menu bar. - Facilitates clearer inspection of suit fitting. ### Multidirectional Grid Optimization Tool - Located in the attribute editor for buttons, copies, pull-heads, pull pieces, and straight buttons (excluding lines). - Two optimization types: 1. **Mesh Grid Type**: Reduces grid line count for optimization. - Input grid number to control density. - Minimum recommended grid count is 800 to avoid quality loss. - Maximum limited to original mesh count. 2. **Bare-Board Flat Type**: Converts object to flat image for file size reduction.
